notes.claim: A resultant vector is the vector that results from adding two or more vectors together.
Vectors cannot be added by adding their magnitudes, so combining two forces needs their directions as well.
The equilibrant has the same magnitude as the resultant but the opposite direction, so it balances the forces.
Components can be added separately, which gives the resultant part by part.

sources.title: 16.1: Vectors - Engineering LibreTexts
sources.quote: In contrast with scalar quantities, we cannot add, subtract, multiply or divide them by simply adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing the magnitudes.

sources.title: Subtracting vectors - Using vector components - National 5 Maths Revision - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Vector components describe the separate x, y and z values of a vector. When working with vectors, components can be added or subtracted separately.
